arxiv-1311-3407.title: Half-metallicity and giant magneto-optical Kerr effect in N-doped NaTaO 3
arxiv-1311-3407.creator: Y. Saeed 1 , N. Singh 1,2 , and U. Schwingenschlgl 1
arxiv-1311-3407.description: Abstract We employ density functional theory using the modified Becke-Johnson (mBJ) approach to investigate the electronic and magneto-optical properties of N-doped NaTaO 3 . The mBJ results reveal a half metallic nature of NaTaO 2 N, in contrast to results obtained by the generalized gradient approximation. We find a giant polar Kerr rotation of 2.

arxiv-2108-07844.title: Extensions in Jacobian algebras via punctured skein relations Thanks: MSC2020: 16G20, 16E30, 13F60 The first author works for the University Anáuhac and has received travel grants from said institution during this project. The second author worked for the University of Glasgow while writing this art
arxiv-2108-07844.creator: Salomón Domínguez - Ana García Elsener
arxiv-2108-07844.description: Abstract . Given a Jacobian algebra arising from the punctured disk, we show that all non-split extensions can be found using the tagged arcs and skein relations previously developed in cluster algebras theory. Our geometric interpretation can be used to find non-split extensions over other Jacobian algebras arising from surfaces with punctures.

He was also partially s
arxiv-2109-09106.creator: Daniel Faraco, Sauli Lindberg, László Székelyhidi, Jr
arxiv-2109-09106.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Daniel Faraco, Sauli Lindberg, László Székelyhidi, Jr. We revisit the issue of conservation of magnetic helicity and the Woltjer-Taylor relaxation theory in magnetohydrodynamics in the context of weak solutions. We introduce a relaxed system for the ideal MHD system, which decouples the effects of hydrodynamic turbulence such as the appearance of a Reynolds stress term from the magnetic helicity conservation in a manner consistent with observations in plasma turbulence.

arxiv-2312-03159.title: Robust quantisation of circular photogalvanic effect in multiplicative topological semimetals
arxiv-2312-03159.creator: Adipta Pal, Dániel Varjas, Ashley M. Cook
arxiv-2312-03159.description: Abstract Nonlinear response signatures are increasingly recognized as useful probes of condensed matter systems, in particular for characterisation of topologically non-trivial states. The circular photogalvanic effect (CPGE) is particularly useful in study of topological semimetals, as the CPGE tensor quantises for well-isolated topological degeneracies in strictly linearly-dispersing band structures.

arxiv-2503-02798.title: Spike-and-Slab Posterior Sampling in High Dimensions
arxiv-2503-02798.creator: Syamantak Kumar, Purnamrita Sarkar, Kevin Tian, Yusong Zhu
arxiv-2503-02798.description: Abstract Posterior sampling with the spike-and-slab prior [ MB88 ] , a popular multimodal distribution used to model uncertainty in variable selection, is considered the theoretical gold standard method for Bayesian sparse linear regression [ CPS09 , Roc18 ] . However, designing provable algorithms for performing this sampling task is notoriously challenging.

arxiv-2503-23373.title: On the fundamental group of the regular part of Fujiki’s compact Kähler symplectic orbifolds
arxiv-2503-23373.creator: Shun Yamaguchi
arxiv-2503-23373.description: Abstract We calculate the fundamental group of the regular part of certain compact Kähler symplectic orbifolds constructed by Fujiki, called Fujiki’s examples. We determine which one is an irreducible symplectic orbifold among Fujiki’s examples. This answers a question posed in [ 9 ] . 1 Introduction Symplectic orbifolds and related notions First, we define symplectic orbifolds and related notions.

arxiv-2511-17609.title: 3D Ground Truth Reconstruction from Multi-Camera Annotations Using UKF
arxiv-2511-17609.creator: Linh Van Ma 1 , Unse Fatima 1 , Tepy Sokun Chriv 1 , Haroon Imran 1 , Moongu Jeon 1
arxiv-2511-17609.description: Abstract Accurate 3D ground truth estimation is critical for applications such as autonomous navigation, surveillance, and robotics. This paper introduces a novel method that uses an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to fuse 2D bounding box or pose keypoint ground truth annotations from multiple calibrated cameras into accurate 3D ground truth.

arxiv-2512-01678.title: Morphling: Fast, Fused, and Flexible GNN Training at Scale
arxiv-2512-01678.creator: Anubhab Rupesh Nasre anubhavkhajuria5@gmail.com rupesh@cse.iitm.ac.in IIT Madras , India IIT Madras , India
arxiv-2512-01678.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) present a fundamental hardware challenge by fusing irregular, memory-bound graph traversals with regular, compute-intensive dense matrix operations. While frameworks such as PyTorch Geometric (PyG) and Deep Graph Library (DGL) prioritize high-level usability, they fail to address these divergent execution characteristics.

arxiv-2512-06752.title: Multi-Scale Protein Structure Modelling with Geometric Graph U-Nets
arxiv-2512-06752.creator: Chang LiuUniversity of Cambridge cl962@cantab.ac.uk, Vivian LiUniversity of Cambridge vdl21@cam.ac.uk Linus LeongUniversity of Cambridge yhll2@cantab.ac.uk Vladimir RadenkovicUniversity of Cambridge vr375@cam.ac.uk Pietro LiòUniversity of Cambridge pl219@cam.ac.uk Chaitanya K. JoshiUniversity of Cam
arxiv-2512-06752.description: Abstract Geometric Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) and Transformers have become state-of-the-art for learning from 3D protein structures. However, their reliance on message passing prevents them from capturing the hierarchical interactions that govern protein function, such as global domains and long-range allosteric regulation. In this work, we argue that the network architecture itself should mirror this biological hierarchy.

arxiv-2512-09836.title: Fast Factorized Learning
arxiv-2512-09836.creator: Bernhard Stöckl, Maximilian E. Schüle
arxiv-2512-09836.description: Abstract . Learning models over factorized joins avoids redundant computations by identifying and pre-computing shared cofactors. Previous work has investigated the performance gain when computing cofactors on traditional disk-based database systems. Due to the absence of published code, the experiments could not be reproduced on in-memory database systems. This work describes the implementation when using cofactors for in-database factorized learning.

pmc-11351330.creator: Lingxia Chen, Lijun Wang, Lifu Ma, Chao Wang, Xinshu Qin, Minlong Wang, Xiaohe Zhang, Ruoyan Yang, Bing Fang, Jie An, Daniela Tofani
pmc-11351330.description: The incorporation of antioxidants in food products is essential to prevent or delay deterioration, thereby addressing food spoilage. This study investigates the potential enhancement of thiol antioxidant capacity through the addition of a soluble, low-toxic inorganic Sm-cluster.

pmc-11574180.title: Complex charge density waves in simple electronic systems of two-dimensional III2–VI3 materials
pmc-11574180.creator: Yu-Ting Huang, Zhen-Ze Li, Nian-Ke Chen, Yeliang Wang, Hong-Bo Sun, Shengbai Zhang, Xian-Bin Li
pmc-11574180.description: Charge density wave (CDW) is the phenomenon of a material that undergoes a spontaneous lattice distortion and modulation of the electron density. Typically, the formation of CDW is attributed to Fermi surface nesting or electron-phonon coupling, where the CDW vector (QCDW) corresponds to localized extreme points of electronic susceptibility or imaginary phonon frequencies.

pmc-11686669.creator: William B. Cohen, Edward S. Hur, Laura Quigley, Anastasia K. Skipor, Johnny L. Lin, Simon Lee, Joshua J. Jacobs, Daniel D. Bohl
pmc-11686669.description: Category:Ankle Arthritis; Basic Sciences/BiologicsIntroduction/Purpose:Wear debris from metal implants can result in local and systemic complications and has become a growing concern. Potential complications include implant loosening, peri-implant osteolysis, adverse local tissue reaction with destruction of surrounding soft tissues, and end-organ deposition leading to cardiac and neurologic compromise.

pmc-12712501.title: Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Using a Tibial-Pedicled Quadrupled Semitendinosus Autograft With Dual Adjustable-Loop Cortical Suspension
pmc-12712501.creator: Joaquim Rodeia, Rita Alçada, Francisco Baptista, Rodrigo Goes
pmc-12712501.description: Anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction is one of the most commonly performed procedures in knee surgery. Despite its frequency, numerous technical variations exist, and several aspects remain controversial. Hamstring tendons are among the most frequently used autografts, and there is growing interest in techniques that preserve the gracilis tendon.

pmc-13155507.title: Sequential effects in reaching reveal efficient coding in motor planning
pmc-13155507.creator: Tianhe Wang, Yifan Fang, David Whitney
pmc-13155507.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The nervous system uses prior information to enhance movement accuracy, yet the underlying computational mechanisms remain relatively unclear. Prevailing motor control models emphasize Bayesian inference, where prior information is integrated to optimally estimate the current state. An alternative framework, efficient coding, proposes that the system dynamically reallocates encoding resources on the basis of environmental statistics—a mechanism highlighted in perception while underappreciated in motor control. We compared these frameworks in reaching movements, focusing on how the system leverages short-term priors in unpredictable environments.

pmc-13594258.title: XPO1-mediated TRIM21 nuclear export reprograms TREM2+ macrophage polarization by targeting IRF3 to augment anti-PD-1 efficacy in small cell lung cancer
pmc-13594258.creator: Qingwu Du, Tingting Qin, Jingya Wang, Yantao Jiang, Qi Xu, Xueyang Li, Huiyan Liu, Junjie Yu, Yi Lu, Luyao Tong, Tao Sun, Peng Chen, Richeng Jiang, Dingzhi Huang
pmc-13594258.description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy that responds poorly to immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy, due to its immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Here, we analyse preclinical mouse tumor models and patient-derived SCLC samples and identify Exportin 1 (XPO1) as a regulator of immune suppression in SCLC.
